notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: no hardware run was made and the sim backend (gymnasium.make("MiniWorld-Maze-v0")) was not run. The real environment needs numpy, pyglet and an OpenGL context (miniworld/miniworld.py:507-518), so the fake backend is the package's own pure Python kinematic stand-in and was not compared with the upstream environment. The real observation is a 60 x 80 x 3 rendered RGB image (miniworld/miniworld.py:473-474 and :488-491); the fake returns a 3 x 4 x 3 (36-value) coarse RGB stand-in and the fidelity gaps name it. The fake also does not generate the 8x8 room maze, walls or collision geometry, and places the red box 1.5 m ahead of the agent (test data). The only limits are the action space the Gymnasium bridge derives from Discrete(3) (action.index 0 to 2) plus the catalogue constraints on ticks and the reset seed; there is no operator-required bound. Expected warnings for this family: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (it only sets the next reset seed, so it makes no native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the integer inputs ticks, action.index and the two seed inputs. Only cap.world.* catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue requests. gate.digest is the digest the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
